newsitem.title: CANADA: New Canada minister does not foresee carbon tax.
newsitem.headline: New Canada minister does not foresee carbon tax.

text.p: Canada's new natural resources minister, Ralph Goodale, said on Wednesday it was important to meet the country's obligations on limiting climate change but that he did not foresee the introduction of a carbon tax.
He made remarks to reporters shortly after being sworn in as part of a cabinet shuffle. Asked if he anticipated a carbon tax, he said: "No."
Goodale replaced Anne McLellan, an Albertan who had curried favor with her province's energy industry.

Asked about his approach to issues like greenhouse gases, emissions believed to raise world temperatures, Goodale said: "My approach to these issues in the past, as they have come before the cabinet committee or the cabinet itself, has been very consistent with Anne McLellan's approach.
"So I would be following very much in the same vein."
Regarding climate change, he said: "We obviously have important obligations internationally, we have important obligations to ourselves nationally.

"It's important to respect and honor those obligations, but it's also important to be practical and constructive in the way that we do it to ensure good results and at the same time a very strong and positive working relationship with all the players on all sides of the equation."
Asked if this might mean higher energy taxes, he replied: "No, I'm definitely not forecasting that."
